subject: Follow-up: Hosted evaluation access and deployment-mode decision items
messages:
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@finlytics.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick demo recap + hosted evaluation next steps

Hi Oliver / Alicia —

Thanks again for the time earlier — appreciated the walkthrough of the FinLytics ML pipeline and the two primary inference flows (batch scoring for nightly reports + real-time summarization for customer support). This is a quick recap of what we discussed and the action items I promised to follow up on for a hosted evaluation (so we can validate fit before we talk Dedicated / Private options):

Summary of needs you raised:
- Real-time summarization: ~200 TPS peaks, ~30 concurrent requests typical, median request size ~120 tokens in, ~450 tokens out.
- Nightly batch scoring: ~10M tokens per run, runs over a 2–3 hour window.
- Data sensitivity: user transcripts may include low-to-medium sensitivity PII; compliance team will want SOC2 evidence and controls around retention.
- Residency: US-first; EU later if we expand.

Hosted evaluation proposal (what Redwood can do immediately):
1) Sandbox endpoints on our Hosted tier (no infra commitment) — we can provision separate sandbox endpoints for your real-time and batch flows.
2) Default baseline rate limits for the trial: 5 rps steady for real-time endpoint, burst to 25 rps during demo windows; batch endpoint can be run as scheduled jobs (we'll provide throughput guidance to avoid throttling).
3) Token and sequence guidance: recommend client-side prompt truncation to 1024 tokens; we will surface cost/latency per 1k tokens in the console.
4) Security & compliance: we will share SOC2 artifact links and a short evidence package; hosted data retention defaults to 30 days for sandbox logs (we can shorten on request).

Action items I can own this week:
- Share the hosted evaluation checklist + sandbox provisioning guide (attaching hostedeval checklist).
- Provision two sandbox endpoints and creds (expected: 48 business hours).
- Provide a suggested traffic-run plan to exercise batching and prefetch/KV cache behavior.
- Connect Monica (Customer Ops) with your compliance contact for the SOC2 packet.

Questions for you (short answers will help speed provisioning):
- Do you need payloads redaction or zero-storage for the eval (yes/no)?
- Is procurement expecting a copy of the master agreement up front? I attached a draft MA you can review internally.
- For the real-time flow, is 25 rps burst sufficient for your demo peak?

I'll follow up with the checklist and links shortly. If it looks like you need tighter data controls or an SLA-backed throughput target, we'll scope Dedicated or Private VPC as the next step, but the Hosted sandbox is the fastest way to validate latency/cost.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: finlytics-ma-template.pdf, hosted-eval-checklist.xlsx
From: Oliver Park <oliver@finlytics.ai>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia@finlytics.ai>, procure@finlytics.ai
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick demo recap + hosted evaluation next steps

Maya — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below and a couple of asks from procurement/compliance.

On your questions:
- Payload storage: for the evaluation our compliance team would prefer zero storage (no request payloads persisted) if possible; otherwise short retention (7 days) with clear deletion on request.
- MA: yes, procurement would like a redlined MA to start — I copied procure@ on this thread.
- Burst: 25 rps should be fine for the demo; we may push to 40 rps for a stress window but can schedule that with your team.

Other notes:
- SOC2 evidence: can you share a link to the SOC2 report and any standard security questionnaire answers (SSQ, security whitepaper)?
- Network: we need to confirm egress IPs for allowlisting.
- Billing: can we run the sandbox on a limited credit for up to 30 days? That would let our engineering team run the nightly batch without procurement committing yet.

Thanks — we generally prefer to validate on Hosted to get to working integration quickly; we'll escalate to Dedicated or VPC if retention/controls/SLA needs require it.

>

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <oliver@finlytics.ai>, Alicia Gomez <alicia@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2029 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted sandbox access + compliance checklist and next steps

Oliver / Alicia —

Per your reply I put together a compact action plan so we can get the hosted sandbox running with the retention settings you requested and the procurement items started: 

Plan (what will happen next):
1) Zero-storage sandbox mode: we can enable a no-persist mode for sandbox traffic (request/response payloads not written to logs). Please confirm "zero-storage" preference — we will schedule the change when sandbox is ready.
2) Sandbox provisioning: we will provision two endpoints (real-time + batch) and send credentials via our secure secrets link. ETA 48 business hours from confirmation.
3) Rate window: default trial limits will be 5 rps steady / 25 rps burst; if you want a scheduled stress window at 40 rps please propose a 1-hour window and we'll temporarily lift the burst.
4) SOC2 & evidence: Monica will send SOC2 summary, an SSQ export, and a short security whitepaper once I cc her in.
5) Allowlisting: we will provide the full egress IP list and headend domains; please provide the IP whitelist contacts on your side.
6) Procurement/MA: Ben is joining to own commercial coordination — Ben, suggested next step is to share a redline; FinLytics, please have procurement confirm the contact who will accept the redline.

Attachments and links: I attached the hosted-eval-checklist.xlsx (quick runbook) and the MA template. I also added a short HubSpot card to track the sandbox milestone (link below).

Small operational checklist for your engineers (to speed the first hour):
- Add our egress IPs to your allowlist (we'll send these in the provisioning email).
- Add a simple retry/backoff for 429s in the client (we'll provide recommended retry policy).
- For the batch run, use our bulk ingest pattern and parallel chunking to avoid token-size throttles.

If that plan looks good please confirm 1) zero-storage=yes/no and 2) a preferred stress window time (if you want 40 rps). Once we have that I'll trigger provisioning and send the secrets link.

Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.ai

Attachments: hosted-eval-checklist.xlsx, finlytics-ma-template.pdf
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/FinLytics

Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Hosted evaluation access and deployment-mode decision items

Maya / Ben —

Thanks — zero-storage=yes. Please enable no-persist for the sandbox. For the stress window let's do Friday 19 Jul 2029 14:00–15:00 PT at 40 rps so we can validate autoscaling behavior.

Procurement: I'll loop in our contracting lead to pick up the MA redline; please send your standard redline to procure@finlytics.ai and I'll make introductions.

Looking forward to the sandbox — please send the credentials and IPs when ready.

—Oliver
Head of Platform Engineering | FinLytics
